problem.heading:
Air complaints. Water leaks.
Events that need a response.
problem.intro: A building contains different rooms, activities and services. Link each issue to the measurements and operating record that can help explain it.

cards.title: Recurring room complaints
cards.body: Stuffy meetings, uneven temperatures and changing use need room-level evidence. Compare air conditions with the ventilation and occupancy schedule before changing the whole floor.

cards.title: Moisture in the wrong place
cards.body: Humid interiors, condensate and plumbing leaks require different observations. Pair environmental readings with water-contact points where vulnerable equipment or contents justify them.

cards.title: Conditions without a clear next step
cards.body: A room reading or water event needs the correct location, report time and responsible team. Compare it with equipment feedback and maintenance records to decide what to check next.

problem.takeaway: Identify the affected room, select the relevant measurements and give the responsible team a specific investigation task.

focus.heading:
Give every zone
a useful monitoring plan.
focus.intro: Measure conditions where people or vulnerable assets are affected. Add service context only when it helps determine the next action.

stages.title: Define the zone
stages.body: Map room use, ventilation, water services and vulnerable equipment. Separate spaces that behave differently.

stages.title: Choose complementary points
stages.body: Match room air, water contacts and selected gas points to the zone. Use light and motion readings where they help explain room-use patterns.

stages.title: Connect status and permitted control
stages.body: Read approved equipment and meter signals. Use a commissioned IoT Controller interface for permitted lighting, ventilation or water-service commands.

stages.title: Review the intervention
stages.body: Confirm equipment feedback and compare conditions after the action. Record rejected commands, recurring faults and completed work.

focus.note: Dedicated fire and gas protection remain responsible for their alarm and emergency functions. Operational commands use approved equipment interfaces with local priority.
focus.detailTitle: How to make room comparisons meaningful
focus.detail: Use representative air positions and avoid direct breath, supply jets and heat sources. Distinguish ambient pressure from differential pressure. PIR indicates detected motion, not headcount. Treat water-contact points as a separate coverage layout. Compare readings with known room use and equipment schedules; verify interface timestamps before combining systems. A high CO₂ value may justify a ventilation review, while a water event requires a different callout. Keep these response rules distinct.

applications.heading:
A different plan
for each occupied space.
applications.intro: Prioritise rooms with recurring concerns, varied use or vulnerable services. Expand the measurement set around the actual operating problem.

platform.heading:
The room, the services
and the next action.
platform.intro: 4G sensors send their measured data directly to Hitelecom Cloud or the agreed receiving platform. Add selected meter records and a defined HD20 or HR-10 equipment interface where the operating task requires them.
platform.insight: Review the room schedule and ventilation record. Water-contact events use a separate location and response rule.

steps.title: Locate the affected zone
steps.body: Review the relevant air, climate or water event with its timestamp and device status.

steps.title: Respond through the right system
steps.body: Assign the callout or send a permitted operational command through the configured equipment interface.

steps.title: Verify state, then outcome
steps.body: Check actual run / stop or position feedback independently of the command. Review the affected room and record completed work.

platform.channels: 4G sensors report directly to the receiving platform. Select NB-IoT or a compatible LoRa gateway path only for the corresponding supplied configuration.
platform.boundary: A command acknowledgement is not proof of equipment operation. Commission permissions, local override, loss-of-communication behaviour and independent equipment feedback.

deployment.heading:
Start with a representative zone.
Make the comparison repeatable.

steps.title: Survey rooms and services
steps.body: Map room issues, water paths, gas-specific needs, meters and permitted control interfaces.

steps.title: Commission each measurement
steps.body: Verify sensor readings, wet / recovery events, device identities, equipment feedback and command handling.

steps.title: Agree the facilities workflow
steps.body: Set separate review and notification rules for air, climate, water and missing data; assign the responsible teams.

acceptance: Room and service-zone IDs match the site plan.
Ordered sensor channels, water-detection coverage and configured equipment points are confirmed.
Sensor reports and agreed external inputs retain their timestamps.
Assigned staff can receive, investigate and close a test event.
Permitted commands, actual feedback, local priority and communication-loss behaviour are tested.

faq.q: What does a Smart Buildings monitoring plan include?
faq.a: Start with the building’s actual risks and operating tasks: air and climate in occupied rooms, water contacts near vulnerable services, and selected equipment or meter feedback. Add CO or another specific gas only where the site assessment calls for it. Each zone needs a useful set, not every sensor.

faq.q: Does a CO₂ reading show whether a room is safe?
faq.a: CO₂ can support a ventilation review in suitable occupied spaces, but it does not describe every pollutant or establish safe air. Interpret its pattern with room use and ventilation. For a specific chemical or process concern, select the appropriate measurement and assessment method with the responsible specialist.

faq.q: Can the same device provide every measurement?
faq.a: No. The ordered air-quality configuration provides its selected room channels. H Series water-leak devices monitor separate sensing locations. Metering, door states and permitted control actions use separately selected instruments and controller interfaces. Give every point a clear purpose and source.

faq.q: Does PIR measure occupancy or provide personnel protection?
faq.a: PIR records detected motion within its coverage. It is not a reliable headcount or a personnel-protection function. Use it as activity context where suitable. People counting, access control, fire detection and emergency systems require their own appropriate equipment and responsibilities.

faq.q: Can this connect to our BMS and control the HVAC?
faq.a: Yes, through a defined and commissioned interface. HD20 offers a 4DO + 4DI + 4AI reference configuration for compatible commands, state feedback and measurements; HR-10 provides selected serial or current-loop connections. Allocate the actual points, electrical interfaces and protocols. Check local priority, permissions and returned equipment state; do not directly switch a load beyond the supplied output rating.

faq.q: How do water events and air-quality notifications differ?
faq.a: They answer different questions and need different response rules. A water-contact event should identify the sensing position and the duty team’s callout procedure. An air or climate trend normally needs context before an intervention. Commission both workflows, including what staff should do when reports are missing.

faq.q: Does air-quality monitoring replace fire detection?
faq.a: No. CO₂, particles, TVOC and room-temperature measurements are not a dedicated fire-detection system. This solution uses sensor data reporting, including direct 4G transmission; fire-alarm panel integration is not included. Fire detection, local warning and emergency response remain separate building provisions.

faq.q: Which extra points are useful in parking and service areas?
faq.a: Select CO or other gas channels from the actual vehicle, fuel or process exposure. Add water contacts near vulnerable plumbing, compatible door switches for service access, and meters for circuits the operator needs to review. Gas detector duties, metering accuracy and switch interfaces require specific selection; none is implied by an indoor air sensor alone.
